subject: math.GM
name: Riemann hypothesis
statement: Every nontrivial zero of the analytically continued Riemann zeta function ζ(s) has real part 1/2.
importance: Controls the finest expected error bounds in the distribution of prime numbers.
status_note: Computations and partial zero-density results do not establish the assertion for every nontrivial zero.

subject: math.GM
name: P versus NP
statement: Is every decision problem whose yes-instances have certificates checkable in polynomial time also solvable by a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm? Equivalently, is P=NP?
importance: A foundational question about the power of efficient computation.
status_note: NP-completeness and restricted-model lower bounds do not separate P from NP.

references.title: Clay Mathematics Institute: P vs NP

subject: math.GM
name: Collatz conjecture
statement: Starting from any positive integer, repeatedly divide an even value by 2 and replace an odd value n by 3n+1. The resulting sequence eventually reaches 1.
importance: An accessible iteration problem exposing the limits of current arithmetic-dynamical methods.
status_note: Almost-all and extensive computational results do not establish the assertion for every starting integer.

subject: math.GM
name: Strong Goldbach conjecture
statement: Every even integer greater than 2 is the sum of two prime numbers, with repetition allowed.
importance: A foundational additive-prime problem whose elementary statement has resisted centuries of work.
status_note: The three-prime weak Goldbach theorem is proved; the two-prime assertion remains open.

subject: math.GM
name: Twin prime conjecture
statement: There are infinitely many primes p for which p+2 is also prime.
importance: The simplest fixed-gap prediction for the distribution of primes.
status_note: Bounded gaps between primes are proved, but an infinitely recurring gap of exactly 2 is not.

subject: math.GM
name: Odd perfect number problem
statement: Does there exist an odd positive integer equal to the sum of its positive proper divisors? Equivalently, can an odd integer n satisfy σ(n)=2n?
importance: Extends the ancient study of perfect numbers beyond the understood even case.
status_note: No example is known; large lower bounds and strong restrictions do not rule out all odd candidates.

subject: math.GM
name: Perfect cuboid problem
statement: Do positive integers a,b,c exist for which a²+b², a²+c², b²+c², and a²+b²+c² are all perfect squares?
importance: A classical Diophantine problem with a concrete geometric interpretation.
status_note: Integer boxes with all three face diagonals integral exist; requiring the space diagonal too remains unresolved.

subject: math.GM
name: Lonely runner conjecture
statement: For k+1 runners starting together at one point and moving at distinct constant speeds around a unit-length circular track, does each runner at some time have circular distance at least 1/(k+1) from every other runner?
importance: Connects an elementary motion puzzle to Diophantine approximation and discrete geometry.
status_note: The conjecture is proved for several small values of k; arbitrary numbers of runners remain open.

subject: math.GM
name: Hadwiger–Nelson problem
statement: What is the minimum number of colors needed to color every point of the Euclidean plane so that points at distance exactly 1 always receive different colors?
importance: A basic accessible question linking geometry and infinite graph coloring.
status_note: The chromatic number of the plane is known to be at least 5 and at most 7; its exact value is open.

subject: math.GM
name: Erdős–Straus conjecture
statement: For every integer n≥2, do positive integers x,y,z exist such that 4/n=1/x+1/y+1/z? The denominators need not be distinct.
importance: A classic Egyptian-fraction question combining elementary arithmetic and Diophantine equations.
status_note: Many congruence classes and extensive finite ranges are verified; no proof covers every n.
